title: Bust Candidates
brief: Which players are likely to finish below their expected auction price in our 9-cat league, and why (role loss, crowded usage, shooting regression, age)? It must say that a bust label is about price, so each line should give a price at which the player becomes fine to buy.
summary: In our league a bust is a player whose price is wrong, not a player to avoid. The clearest busts are the five guards and forwards priced as first-rounders (Cunningham, Mitchell, Maxey, Jalen Johnson, Haliburton) and a group of mid-round names like Trae Young, Booker, Brunson, Holmgren and the young centers. Each of them becomes a fine buy at the lower price given in his line. Set a maximum bid for each one before 2026-10-18, let others pay above it, and check the early-season signs listed for role loss, shooting regression and age.

sections.heading: A bust label is about price

paragraphs.text: Calling a player a bust does not mean you skip him. It means the market values him wrongly at his current price. The same player can be a fade in round one and a fine buy later. Your call depends on his price, not on whether you like him.

A label only means something in its format. For us that means 9-cat H2H with 144 players drafted. A high ESPN rank or a big price in our league last season is not a reason to pay. In every line below, the real question is whether his projected 9-cat line justifies the price. Before the draft, write down a maximum bid for each name. Then stop at that number.

Play the prediction game with the top names. Cade Cunningham gets his value from assists but gives it back in turnovers, and his FG% and FT% are only middling. That makes him a 6th to 10th category player at about 45 to 50 USD. Donovan Mitchell is not a first-rounder to any expert, so the low to mid 30s is the target. Tyrese Maxey projects around 15th to 19th, so he is worth about 40 to 45 USD.

When a team adds high-usage players, the existing star loses usage and assist upside even if his minutes stay the same. The same happens when a scorer moves next to other ball-dominant players. Check usage and assists in the first two weeks, not just minutes.

Examples in our pool: Jalen Johnson should lose assists, FG% and steals next to McCollum, so stop at about 35 to 40 USD. Mitchell and Harden share the ball in Cleveland. Maxey shares it with Brown, LeBron and Embiid. Trae Young now plays next to Davis and Dybantsa. Siakam's assists should drop with Haliburton back. Booker may play off the ball next to Jalen Green.

Be wary of value that came from teammates being out. Trey Murphy's role last season came with Murray out, so above 25 USD you are paying for a role that is gone. Andrew Nembhard is an assists-only guard now that Haliburton is back. Draft him for 1 USD at most, or add him off waivers only if Haliburton sits.

When many players on one team have career years at once, expect some of them to regress, often all at once. Treat hot shooting and steal rates from last season as the high end of the range, not the median.

Watch these names: Jamal Murray's 42 to 43% from three is expected back near 40 to 41%. Mitchell had a career-best two-point percentage and 1.5 steals. Walker Kessler's threes and steals came from a five-game sample, so do not go much past 15 USD. Dejounte Murray, Ayo Dosunmu and Shaedon Sharpe all had steals from a lucky deflection-to-steal rate.

Regression does not always make a bust. Nickeil Alexander-Walker's second-half shooting will cool. But his projection already includes that and still has no weak category, so he is a value near 15 to 20 USD. The test is the price, not the regression flag.

A long-time veteran turning 29 or older is probably who he is. He is not due for a breakout. Projections are a median. When two players project the same, take the one with the wider range, because veterans like Tobias Harris have no realistic path above their projection.

For older stars the risk is games played and rest, not per-game skill. Stephen Curry (38) played 43 games and has a knee issue, so bid 25 to 31 USD. Harden (37) is a low to mid 20s buy and has a two-game finals week. Anthony Davis (33) is fair at 26 to 30 USD, not at last season's price. LeBron (42) is fair at 20 to 25 USD.

Sometimes the market has already priced age in. Kyrie Irving and Damian Lillard carry age flags, but their market prices are low. That makes them value targets, not busts, at the prices in their lines.

Kevin Durant splits opinion. Most experts see him as a late first-round pick in 9-cat, and our room should pay about 40 to 46 USD. Josh found 40 USD too rich for a 37-year-old after heavy minutes, and the median-only view of veterans backs that caution. If you buy him, stay near 40 USD and check in week one whether he plays 35 to 36 minutes or nearer 33.

sections.heading: Draft day and early season plan

paragraphs.text: At the auction, let others pay first-round money for Cunningham, Mitchell, Maxey, Jalen Johnson and Haliburton. Haliburton is coming off a torn Achilles and has a 3-4-3 playoff schedule, so his ceiling is the mid-to-high 30s. Spend the savings on players whose market price is already below their fair price.

If a bust candidate lands on your team, check the listed early signs in the first two to three weeks: usage next to the new teammates, minutes, and whether hot shooting holds. If the role loss is real, sell before the 2027-03-04 deadline. A weak schedule in weeks 19 to 21 is another reason to sell.
